questions.text: How did the weakness come on — was it sudden or gradual, and is it confined to specific muscle groups or generalised throughout the body?
questions.purpose: Sudden focal weakness suggests neurological cause; gradual generalised weakness suggests systemic, metabolic, or myopathic aetiology
options: Sudden onset, focal (one side, one limb, one area)

questions.text: Did the weakness start suddenly and is it associated with facial drooping, speech difficulty, or vision changes?
questions.purpose: Sudden focal weakness with these features is a stroke presentation requiring immediate emergency assessment

questions.text: Have you also experienced shortness of breath, chest pain, or palpitations alongside the weakness?
questions.purpose: Cardiorespiratory compromise presenting as weakness requires urgent cardiac and respiratory assessment

questions.text: Have you had any recent viral illness, diarrhoea, or infection before the weakness developed?
questions.purpose: Post-infectious ascending weakness following GI illness may suggest Guillain-Barré syndrome

questions.text: Do you have known diabetes, kidney disease, or take medications that affect electrolytes?
questions.purpose: Metabolic causes such as hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, or uraemia commonly cause generalised weakness

questions.text: Have you noticed difficulty swallowing, double vision, drooping eyelids, or slurred speech?
questions.purpose: Bulbar and ocular features alongside weakness suggest myasthenia gravis or other neuromuscular junction disease

questions.text: Have you had unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or night sweats — which could indicate an underlying malignancy?
questions.purpose: Constitutional symptoms with weakness may indicate paraneoplastic syndrome or cancer-related weakness
